title: WordPress Apply: the title and description a theme keeps per page in its own metas are the customer's, child themes and copies included
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/brief-wordpress.test.mjs

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail' lines and the result of each case whose name starts with: "the title and the description a theme keeps for each page in metas of its own are said again from the customer's words"; "a theme that keeps no such metas, or a site whose theme cannot be read, is left quietly"; "a child theme's pages are read under the parent's name too, the one whose code prints them"; "the other languages' copies have their title, description and heading said again in their own language".
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 61).

Every named case is 'ok' (none 'not ok', none '# SKIP'): the metas <stylesheet>_document_title and <stylesheet>_metadesc (and the parent's <template>_ prefix for a child theme) of each page are said again from the customer's words, the description as the visible sub-title; a theme with no such metas or an unreadable theme is left quietly; other languages' copies get theirs in their own language.
evidence: Ledger L16, 05/10/2026: after Apply on ja-kinetic (WordPress) <title> read 'Kinetic — Observability, reimagined' and every page's meta description sold the demo: the theme prints both from wp_ja_kinetic_document_title / wp_ja_kinetic_metadesc, which no contract slot holds. Reds 0f7ca8846, 4f546157d; fixes e7b55a88e, 10a589255.
fence: Only the metas the theme itself names are written; nothing is written on a theme that keeps none.

tests: the title and the description a theme keeps for each page in metas of its own are said again from the customer's words
a theme that keeps no such metas, or a site whose theme cannot be read, is left quietly
a child theme's pages are read under the parent's name too, the one whose code prints them
the other languages' copies have their title, description and heading said again in their own language
